decisions.reason: The source specifically requires no-referral rewards to appear in NFT metadata attributes; it does not change the separate reward summary shown in the NFT detail view.
Reward attribution does not change whether NFT metadata and asset endpoints resolve successfully.
The client explicitly requires tickets and commissions from no-referral purchases to appear on the leaderboard, refining its required totals to include that purchase path.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I just completed a mint using 'no referral code' and adding a '$1 tip'.

[ACCOUNT_001] Tipping still isn't working.

[ACCOUNT_001] Tickets and commissions from 'no referral code' purchases are still not appearing on the leaderboard or in the NFT attributes.

Also, after I minted, a second transaction popped up (shown in the screenshot). I cancelled it, but the mint still worked fine.
Do you know why that second transaction appeared? Was it for the tip?

value_updates.ticket_and_commission_totals: The leaderboard must accurately total all prize tickets and commission amounts attributable to completed mints, including purchases made without a referral code.

decisions.reason: The source reports reward-data omissions after a successful mint but does not change which NFTs must appear on the dashboard.
The source names the leaderboard and NFT attributes, not the user's dashboard reward summary.
No-referral ticket and commission visibility on the leaderboard and NFT attributes does not alter the defined public mint, pool, referral, or draw counters.
The source concerns missing reward attributes, not NFT image, cover, wallet-information, or product-view presentation.
The source does not change the NFT's mint-number referral-code identity or where that code is displayed.
The runtime report does not request any change to About-page copy describing no-referral reward allocation.
The source does not address how referral codes, badges, tickets, or book access behave when an NFT is transferred.
Missing no-referral tickets and commissions do not change badge triggers, thresholds, or award destinations.

The candidate already requires random commission allocation for successful no-referral mints; the source concerns visibility of resulting rewards and does not change the allocation rule or resolve its first-mint ambiguity.
